scope: Independent product-utility review of the canonical 76-venue Tokyo universe after TOKYO-ADDRESSABLE-CONVERSION-1B. No venue promotion, range transcription, production artifact change, or release execution.

decisionBasis.notMechanical: The decision is not derived from the 13.2% rate alone and does not treat B/C/D closure or 10/10 conversion as coverage adequacy.

utility.largeLiveArenaDome: FAIL: canonical production contains 0 dome, 0 arena, and 0 venue at or above the review-only 3,000-seat large band.
utility.concertHall: PARTIAL PASS: Suntory Hall, LINE CUBE SHIBUYA, Hamarikyu Asahi Hall, Yurakucho Asahi Hall, and RISURU provide useful choices, but major 3,000+ multipurpose/live halls remain absent.
utility.commercialTheatreMusical25d: PARTIAL PASS: Meijiza, NNTT Playhouse, THEATER MILANO-Za, Sunshine Theatre, and Theater G-Rosso provide real utility, but Tokyo Takarazuka, Shiki theatres, Theatre Orb, ACT, Kabukiza, Nissay, Brillia, and other high-demand MUST venues remain absent.
utility.mediumLiveHouse: FAIL: Zepp, EX THEATER, Toyosu PIT, and comparable live-house candidates are all nonproduction.
utility.otherReservedEvents: PASS WITH GAPS: the broader 53-venue Tokyo production catalog supplies many civic, classical, lecture, and small theatre choices.

clusters.Tama: usable through RISURU and broader civic-hall production
clusters.otherMunicipalTokyo: broadly represented by the noncanonical production catalog

utility.claimFit: An explicit statement that the site offers a verified curated subset would be accurate, but disclosure cannot support a claim that major Tokyo venues are substantially covered while every large arena/dome and all medium live-house candidates are absent.

holdTaxonomy.assessment: The taxonomy is safety-preserving and the fresh A-to-B/C moves are tied to issuer-owned source gaps or exact contradictions rather than release convenience. It is sufficient to prevent unsafe promotion, but not sufficient to turn missing user-visible venues into positive coverage.

evidencePackagingCaveat.impact: These records remain nonproduction and therefore do not weaken production quality, but they reduce the strength of a positive release-coverage claim and should be normalized only in bounded, utility-prioritized work.
